title: Release Test Plan for Auth0
brief: A structured release test plan for the core identity service migration to Auth0.

delegate.scenario: You are a lead backend engineer handing off notes from a sprint planning session to prepare a smoke and integration test plan. The QA automation team and platform engineers will execute these validation procedures during tomorrow night's maintenance window. They need a concise, clear execution document to verify auth flows without causing production downtime.
delegate.inputs:
Sprint 42 handoff notes for Auth0 cutover:
- Target service: Core Identity Provider (us-east-1 cluster)
- OAuth2 endpoints to validate: /oauth/token, /oauth/authorize, /userinfo
- Token expiration: Access tokens set to 3600s, refresh tokens set to 30 days.
- Rate limit threshold: Verify throttling triggers at 500 req/min per client_id.
- Legacy fallback: Route traffic back to Okta v2 if error rate exceeds 2.5% over 5 minutes.
- Service tier dependency table:
| Service | Port | Health Endpoint | Max Latency |
| Auth-Gateway | 8443 | /healthz | 120ms |
| User-Directory | 9090 | /status | 250ms |
| Token-Vault | 8443 | /vault/health | 80ms |
- Rollback trigger: If /oauth/token p99 latency exceeds 300ms or error rate > 5.0% for 3 consecutive minutes, initiate immediate rollback.
- Security validation: Confirm JWT signing algorithm is RS256; reject any tokens signed with HS256.
delegate.goal: Provide QA and DevOps engineers with a prioritized, step-by-step test plan and rollback checklist that ensures safe cutover.

criteria.text: Specifies that the target audience is the on-call QA and platform engineering team.
Directs the AI to organize the procedures into clear chronological testing phases with pass/fail criteria.
Requires verification of security configurations and token signing rules.
Directs the AI to cross-check network and threshold values to flag technical contradictions or port collisions.
Constrains the final output length to under 500 words for operational readability during maintenance.

traps.description: Auth-Gateway and Token-Vault are assigned the exact same port number on the same host configuration.
The fallback and rollback error rate thresholds contradict each other regarding when to revert traffic.
